doc_verification.detail: Constraint qdrant_invariant_delete_invisibility_001 states 'after delete(points), search does not return those points'. OpenAPI documents wait parameter with 'Default is true' (openapi/openapi-snapshots.ytt.yaml:20, 63, 106), but source code (src/common/update.rs:40) uses #[serde(default)] with bool type defaulting to false, creating discrepancy. Documentation promises wait=true by default, implementation defaults to wait=false.

chain_trace.break_detail: Link breaks at documentation-implementation mismatch: OpenAPI (openapi/openapi-snapshots.ytt.yaml) states 'wait parameter default is true', but UpdateParams (src/common/update.rs:40) uses #[serde(default)] which defaults bool to false. Users relying on documented default get wait=false behavior, causing race conditions where search reads stale data before deletion completes. Source confirms: wait: wait.unwrap_or(false) (line 54) for gRPC, and #[serde(default)] for REST both default to false, contradicting docs.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: DELETE request → UpdateParams { wait: bool } with #[serde(default)] → bool defaults to FALSE → deletion queued asynchronously → concurrent SEARCH reads stale index → deleted points visible. No synchronization unless caller explicitly sets wait=true.
source_grounding.note: Source confirms default is false. This is by-design async behavior, but documentation incorrectly states default is true. The defect is the documentation mismatch, not the async behavior itself. However, the invariant violation (32 visible deleted points) stems from this async default being inconsistent with documented promise of immediate visibility.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Documentation-implementation mismatch (wait default). Not environmental or race condition—this is documented as async-by-default behavior but docs promise sync-by-default. The 32 visible deleted points are expected when wait=false, not a race.
